clue.text: It does business in more than one way

definitions.text: It does business in more than one way

parts.words: It does business in more than one way
parts.note: a small local store often stands where two streets meet, so it trades on more than one 'way' or road

explanation.surface: A versatile firm with several lines of trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one way' sounds like several business methods, but it means two roads meeting at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: A local convenience store traditionally sits at a street junction, so it literally does business on two ways.

definitions.meaning: a move to a lower rank or level
an order to quit one's post

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a noun for a reduction in level and a verb meaning to leave a position voluntarily.

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the verb form used for what will happen

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a grammatical tense of verbs and the time that is yet to come.

indicators.note: the iron symbol is opened out, spread apart, to let the numeral in

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A golfer removes the four iron from the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four iron' looks like a golf club, but four is IV and iron is FE; 'taken out' means FE is drawn apart to hold IV.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a cardinal number, the one after four.

clue.text: A quality one considers oneself worthy to have

definitions.text: A quality one considers oneself worthy to have

parts.words: A quality one considers oneself worthy to have
parts.note: read as a description of regarding one's own self as worthy, i.e. having a good opinion of oneself

explanation.surface: A trait a person feels they deserve to possess.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to be about a quality one deserves; it actually describes considering oneself worthy, which is the quality itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-respect, or confidence in one's own worth, is exactly considering oneself worthy.

clue.text: But it's not the time nothing happens

definitions.text: But it's not the time nothing happens

parts.words: But it's not the time nothing happens
parts.note: the time named after nought is in fact the moment a planned operation begins, when everything happens

explanation.surface: A protest that this is no idle moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the hour named 'nothing' is the moment when the action starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheduled start time of a military operation is named with the word for nought, yet it is when action begins.

parts.note: 'evening' read as making things even or smooth, as with creased clothes, rather than night-time

explanation.surface: Someone put in a few hours after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' suggests night shifts, but it means smoothing out, which is what pressing laundry does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes flat with a hot appliance makes them even, so it is literally evening work.

parts.note: refers to the nursery rhyme of the old woman with so many children she did not know what to do, living in footwear

explanation.surface: A packed orphanage struggling for space.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'There was an old woman who lived in a shoe' tells of a woman with too many children in her odd house.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme, the old woman's crowded family lives inside a piece of footwear.

clue.text: Twist or bust, I've to be bold

indicators.note: to twist is to distort, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letters of I've without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A card player's gamble: stick or go bust, you have to be brave.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the card game pontoon, where players say 'twist' or 'bust'; here 'Twist' rearranges OR BUST into OBTRUS, and I've follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bold or brash is conspicuous and pushes itself forward, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Slight change of heart for space traveller

indicators.note: a small rearrangement, so the word's letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small change of mind for an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' reads as a change of mind, but only the letters of heart are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet travels through space in orbit around the Sun, so it is a space traveller.

parts.note: 'main' read as the sea (the briny main), not 'chief', so this is the Roman sea god

explanation.surface: The chief god of the Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'principal', suggesting Jupiter; it is the old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the sea, equivalent to the Greek Poseidon, rules the main.

clue.text: Disposition of uncle to have a fling

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncle's tendency to enjoy a brief affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' reads as temperament, but it means rearranging OF UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling oneself about or move off in an impatient huff is to make an exaggerated, angry movement.

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen a cutting edge, taken loosely as cut

explanation.surface: One river crossed or intersected by another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places the river letter next to the word for cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a major European river flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

parts.note: read as leaving without saying goodbye, rather than the idiom for something obvious

explanation.surface: Something was too obvious to need stating.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'went without saying' means 'was obvious'; read literally it is slipping away without a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee secretly is to depart without telling anyone, literally going off unannounced.

clue.text: They are named for the post

definitions.text: They are named for the post

parts.words: They are named for the post
parts.note: the people whose names are written on letters and parcels, not candidates named for a job

explanation.surface: Candidates nominated for a vacant position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Named for the post' suggests job nominees; it means people named on mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipients of letters are the people whose names appear on the envelope sent by post.

clue.text: Possibly a good tryer? That's somewhat disparaging

indicators.note: the letters may be arranged in another possible order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling someone 'a good trier' can sound like faint praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' signals that A GOOD TRYER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that belittle or slight someone are disparaging in tone.

parts.note: read literally: a conflict lasting about a century, not a famous boxing bout

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxing match billed as the biggest ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fight of the century' is a boxing promoter's phrase; here it is a war lasting over a hundred years, between England and France (1337-1453).
explanation.definitionFit: The long medieval conflict between England and France lasted more than a century.

parts.note: ruddy means reddish in colour
a brick is old British slang for a reliable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A rosy-cheeked decent chap from a particular kind of university.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brick' is old-fashioned British praise for a dependable person.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes the British civic universities founded in industrial cities in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

parts.note: protests made on foot, with 'pedestrian' read as walking rather than dull

explanation.surface: Dull, unexciting demonstrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' suggests uninspired; read as walking, it gives strikes where workers leave on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Strikes in which workers leave their workplace are named for walking off the job.

parts.note: a fanciful hope, imagined as the dreams of someone smoking a pipe (originally of opium)

explanation.surface: A tobacco user's preferred brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' could mean preference, but here it is a fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrealistic hope is named after visions induced by smoking an opium pipe.

definitions.meaning: decorative cord trimming sewn along edges of garments or cakes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lengths of tubing and a decorative edging trim on fabric or icing.

parts.note: taken as written
a lag is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: A criminal locked up during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag' is British slang for a prisoner; the answer is a German POW camp for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Second World War, Germany held captured enemy officers in this kind of prison camp.

clue.text: Do rise above debts admitted to be bad

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: Get above your debts, owning up to them as bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' reads upwards, as fits a down entry, and 'above' puts that piece on top; IOUs are signed notes admitting a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful or repugnant is extremely bad in the moral sense.

clue.text: Aims to get a ship round an awkward pier

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the ship letters go around the rearranged pier

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: something awkward is out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A captain tries to steer a vessel around a tricky jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges PIER into PIRE, and 'round' wraps the steamship's letters about it; 'Aims' is the verb, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim at a goal is to strive toward or hope to achieve it.

clue.text: A record, second highest in the European charts

parts.note: taken as written
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A track sitting at number two in the European hit parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charts' suggests music lists, but it means maps, on which these mountains stand highest.
explanation.definitionFit: The great mountain range of central Europe has the highest peaks on maps of western Europe.

clue.text: Spent money on things like free range eggs

definitions.meaning: eggs produced by hens kept outdoors, read literally as produced outside

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means expended, of money, and literally describes eggs produced by hens outdoors.

definitions.meaning: a key fits and operates this fastening device
a second-row forward in a rugby scrum

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the fastening a key turns and a second-row forward position in rugby union.

clue.text: Police constable holding back in a state of terror

indicators.note: the constable's letters contain the other piece
the words are read in reverse order of letters

explanation.surface: A policeman restraining someone who is terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns IN A into ANI, which PC holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fear is a state of terror.

parts.note: en is French for in
a counter is a bar where drinks or goods are served

explanation.surface: An instruction to rendezvous at a French pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone, especially unexpectedly, is to come across them.
